definition: An organization participating in a business or review process.
An organization supplying goods or services in the reconciliation context.
A legal entity against whose payable account transactions are reconciled.
The account relationship between one supplier and one buyer legal entity.
A business document recording an invoice, adjustment or account statement.
A document requesting payment for supplied goods or services.
A document recording an adjustment that reduces an amount payable under the approved sign policy.
A document recording an adjustment whose payable effect requires an explicit source sign policy.
A supplier-provided statement of account for an explicitly bounded reconciliation scope.
A transfer of funds whose allocation to invoices is recorded separately.
The system or submission channel that produced a source dataset.
An immutable identified snapshot used as reconciliation evidence.
A source-specific assertion about a document or account, preserving values that may disagree with another source.
An invoice-level observation appearing in a supplier statement.
An observation extracted from the buyer accounts-payable dataset.
A dated amount linking a payment or credit to an invoice.
An allocation of a payment amount to an invoice.
An application of part or all of a credit memo to an invoice.
A source-derived net payable balance for an account, currency and cut-off scope.
The account, currency, cut-off and completeness conditions under which records are comparable.
An identified execution context binding input datasets, scope and rule versions.
A versioned semantic specification of a deterministic check, not an executable algorithm.
An explicit decision linking or leaving unmatched source observations with its method and status.
The recorded outcome of applying a rule in a run, including not-evaluable outcomes.
An exception record derived from a failed deterministic rule evaluation; it does not establish recoverability.
An evidence-linked explanation proposed for a finding, distinct from a confirmed review decision.
An attributable human disposition of a finding or proposed interpretation.
A governed value used to classify a status, outcome or interpretation.
A normalized payment-state vocabulary value.
A classification of the discrepancy identified by a deterministic rule.
A vocabulary value distinguishing pass, fail, validation failure and not evaluable.
A workflow state of an audit finding.
A classification of financial or control impact; not an ordinal risk score.
A reviewed or proposed risk rating whose basis must be retained.
A candidate cause classification that does not by itself confirm a root cause.
A human disposition such as confirmed, rejected or needs evidence.
The evidence method used to propose or confirm a source-record correspondence.
